title: Нет Constructions
description: Expressing absence and 'don't have' with нет + genitive
intro: To say 'I don't have' or 'there is no', Russian uses нет followed by the genitive case. This is your first real introduction to the genitive - the case of absence, possession, and 'of'. For now, focus on the pattern: У меня нет + genitive. The genitive endings will become second nature with practice.
rules: У + genitive + нет + genitive = no possession: У меня нет машины. (I don't have a car.)
Нет + genitive = there is no: Здесь нет магазина. (There is no store here.)
Genitive singular: masculine -а/-я (стол → стола), feminine -ы/-и (книга → книги), neuter -а/-я (окно → окна).
After нет, the noun is ALWAYS in genitive - this shows absence.
examples: У меня нет времени. (I don't have time.), время → времени
У него нет брата. (He doesn't have a brother.), брат → брата
Здесь нет воды. (There's no water here.), вода → воды
У нас нет денег. (We don't have money.), деньги → денег

items.explanation: Нет ALWAYS requires genitive case. Сестра is feminine (-а ending), so in genitive it becomes сестры (-а → -ы). Compare: У неё есть сестра (nominative) vs. У неё нет сестры (genitive).
